scope: Offline proposal experiment. No training, deployment or source-artwork edits. Thirty-two controlled synthetic images and forty-two real photographs in two development cohorts.
method: Visible paper determines the lower edges and visible-body coverage. An independent coarse complete-shape estimate proposes and checks the notch. Compare both visible-notch and complete-notch proposals using the same complete-shape support. Never union shape and visible-paper masks.
policy: Retain all 22 supported original baseline real crops exactly. Apply fallback only to 20 rejected inputs; test one-point and two-paper SAM fields, upright plus four covariance orientations. Rank supported proposals using source-only support, never fit error.
syntheticEvaluation: Compare visible-only and separate-shape policies on every original/occluded pair. Exact camera corners enter scoring only. Report normalized corner errors and counts below 1%, 3%, and 5% side length; this uses training geometries and is a perturbation diagnosis, not held-out accuracy.
realEvaluation: Full photo -> frozen crop -> unchanged material mask -> ten-second fitting -> independent export/editor checks. Keep original observation coverage. Occlusion-aware material weighting is deliberately deferred to isolate crop changes. Inspect every new crop and changed export.
limitations: The complete-shape network can be inaccurate or include other objects.
Affine corner construction still cannot generally resolve perspective.
Newly proposed crops require review; a low derived-mask error is not independent crop truth.
